question: Is the difference between diets about absolute size, or about growth rate?
claim: Every chick weighed 39-43 g at day 0; by day 21 chicks had grown 1.8-9.1× that weight; diet medians 3.9-6.8×
n_observations: 578 measurements drawn as 50 per-chick trajectories; each grey line is one chick, no mark is an independent unit
error_bar: no interval is drawn. The bold line is the mean log2 ratio over the chicks measured on that day, so its n falls where follow-up was lost (diet 1: 20 chicks at day 0 to 16 at day 21; diet 4: 10 to 9; diets 2 and 3 constant). Each grey line is one chick
transformations: log2( weight / that same chick's day-0 weight ); 0 = no change (1×), drawn as a dashed line in every panel, and the y ticks give the ratio alongside the log2 value
normalisation_note: dividing by day 0 sets every chick to 0 there by construction, so this figure cannot show a baseline difference even if one existed. Day-0 weights were 39-43 g overall (diet means 40.7-41.4 g), so the normalisation removes almost no between-diet difference; the range is stated in the title because the reader cannot see it

y.baseline_zero: not applicable; 0 is the no-change reference and is drawn

shared_scales: yes; all four panels share both axes by construction (sharex=sharey=True in trajectories_by_group), identical limits and ticks, y tick labels shown once on the left panel

color.redundant_with: panel position and panel title; colour marks only the mean line

excluded: nothing: all 50 chicks and all 578 measurements are drawn, and every chick has a day-0 weight to divide by. Follow-up ended before day 21 for 4 of 20 on diet 1, 0 of 10 on diet 2, 0 of 10 on diet 3, 1 of 10 on diet 4 - that loss is differential across diets, so those trajectories simply stop and the panel titles give both counts
missing: no interior measurements are missing; every chick was weighed at every scheduled day up to its last. Chicks whose follow-up ended early have a line that stops there and is not extended or imputed
